messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@octoanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-02T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — OctoAnalytics

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. OctoAnalytics is evaluating a dedicated pool to serve our production recommendation models (mix of retrieval-augmented generation and dense vector scoring). We expect steady-state traffic of ~6M tokens/day with spiky batch scoring jobs (peak windows where we need sustained throughput for 12–24 hours).

Main ask: can you share packaging options (pool sizes / commit tiers), and a clear H100 vs A100 vs L40S recommendation with perf/$ tradeoffs? Two constraints: we need a 99th-percentile token latency SLO for interactive calls (target <250ms for 512-token responses) and cost predictability for budgeting.

Also attaching our draft MSA for redlines. Can you include any preferred concessions for a 12-month reserved commit?

Thanks,
Elaine
Head of Cloud Ops, OctoAnalytics

Attachment: octo_msa_draft.docx (docx, 128KB)

Hi Elaine — great to meet yesterday. I pulled together three package options and a high-level GPU comparison to help you evaluate cost vs latency risk. High level inlined here; attached is a short proposal PDF with numbers and an example throughput SLA.

Short summary (more detail in attached PDF):
- Small committed pool (8 GPUs) — best for predictable low-throughput, cheaper entry price. Recommended GPU: L40S (48GB) for inference-heavy workloads where perf/$ matters and models are <20B parameters.
- Medium committed pool (32 GPUs) — good balance for mixed interactive + batch. Recommend H100 (80GB) if you need the best mixed-precision throughput and lowest latency on long-context RAG. H100 shows ~1.6–2x throughput vs A100 on our FP16 kernels for the model families you discussed.
- Large committed pool (64+ GPUs) — for high concurrency and mutable workloads. Consider A100 (80GB) if your working sets need maximum memory per model instance (very large context models or multi-model ensembles).

Commit guidance: 12-month term typical. We can provide an up-front discount tiering: 12% for 12-month 8-GPU commit, 18% for 12-month 32-GPU commit, 24% for 12-month 64-GPU commit. Additional 3% if you pre-pay.

SLO note: we propose a throughput-backed SLA (tokens/sec per GPU baseline) rather than rigid per-request latency for batch-heavy workloads; for interactive traffic we'll guarantee 99th-percentile latency under the stated token length by reserving burst capacity for interactive routes.

I've looped in Karthik (pricing) and Marcus (solutions) to validate numbers and packaging.

Soojinn
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

Soojinn / Marcus — quick internal note before we respond with final numbers. Key cost/tech assumptions I used:
- H100 config: 80GB HBM, best for mixed-precision throughput on FP16/AMP; on our stack H100 delivers ~1.7x tokens/sec for long-context RAG vs A100 at similar power draw.
- A100 config: 80GB strong memory for >70B parameter model variants and very large KV caches; latency can be >10–20% worse on some kernels vs H100 but gives headroom for large-model pinning.
- L40S config: 48GB, cheaper per-GPU monthly cost, excellent perf/$ for small-to-medium models (under 30B) and high-batch scoring; less headroom for multi-model ensembles.

Operational impacts:
- For the interactive SLO (<250ms 99p) H100 with dedicated interactive lanes works best at medium pool sizes; using L40S we need more GPUs or a small surge buffer to hit the same 99p due to queueing under burst.
- For batch scoring windows L40S is more cost-efficient if you can accept slightly higher peak run-time.

I recommend we present two priced skews: (A) H100-focused 32-GPU commit (18% discount, 3% prepay bonus) with an interactive burst pool of 4 extra H100s for 99p guarantees; (B) L40S-focused 48-GPU commit (20% discount) optimized for perf/$ with an agreed max batch window latency objective.

If procurement pushes on absolute $/token, we can offer a limited one-time credit (equivalent to 1 month) on contract sign to reduce first-quarter burn. Thoughts?

— Karthik
Director, Pricing

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Agree with Karthik. A couple practical concessions to buy the deal:
- Offer Option A (32x H100) as the primary path. Provide a 14-day free trial of a 4x H100 interactive burst pool (no additional charge) to validate 99p latency before production cutover.
- If Octo prefers perf/$ pricing, offer an L40S 48x baseline with a 4-week runbook to tune batching and kernel selection—offer professional services (2 weeks) at a fixed fee to do the tuning.
- Add an explicit rollover clause: unused monthly committed tokens can be banked up to 2 months to address seasonality.

Operational ask: Hannah, can we confirm whether adding the burst pool requires separate capacity reservation or if we can route from shared spare capacity for the initial trial? Also need a short SLA blurb for the proposal doc.

Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: Capacity & burst pool ops

Quick ops confirmation:
- We can provision a transient 4x H100 burst pool in-host (reserved for trial) without touching the customer's committed units; that's a short-term allocation from our spare pool. Production guarantees require either dedicated reserved burst nodes (if they want guaranteed isolation) or a small dedicated interactive lane (recommended).
- Proposed SLA language for interactive lane: 99th-percentile token latency <250ms for responses <=512 tokens, subject to tokenization and network RTT assumptions. If SLA misses occur due to capacity, we commit to service credits and a remediation plan (scale plan + cost offset).
- Notes on perf/$: for Octo's RAG patterns we see H100 perf gains on long contexts but marginal return past 64 GPUs due to network and batching saturation — helps to call that out in the proposal.

Hannah
Sr. Infrastructure PM — Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — following up with a concise offer that aligns with your constraints. Attached is a short proposal (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf) and the updated MSA with minimal redlines. Below are the two paths we recommend; both assume a 12-month term and annual billing unless you prefer monthly.

Option 1 — H100-focused (recommended for latency-sensitive RAG):
- Baseline: 32x H100 (80GB) dedicated pool
- Discount: 18% off list for 12-month commit; additional 3% if pre-paid in full
- Interactive guarantee: 4x H100 interactive lane reserved (trial available for 14 days at no charge) to meet 99p latency <250ms for responses up to 512 tokens
- Additional: 1-month credit on sign as a one-time concession

Option 2 — L40S-focused (recommended for perf/$ on batch scoring):
- Baseline: 48x L40S dedicated pool
- Discount: 20% off list for 12-month commit; pre-pay bonus negotiable
- Batch SLA: agreed max window latency target for scheduled batch runs; professional services (2 weeks) included to tune batching and kernel selection

Other commercial terms:
- Rollover: allowed up to 2 months for unused committed capacity
- Security/compliance: we can surface SOC2 artifacts and support a short security questionnaire turnaround (3–5 business days)
- Next step: if either option looks good I can circulate an annotated MSA and draft order form.

Would you like us to lock Option 1 pricing and I’ll send a DocuSign link? Happy to run a short trial before you commit.

Best,
Soojin Lee
